question: Prediction of MCI-to-AD conversion (stable against progressive MCI) in ADNI from baseline structural MRI. P-185 uses FreeSurfer regional thickness and volume projected into a learned subspace. P-41 uses 2D slices from three planes, fed to a CNN ensemble with attention. P-41's positive class adds 15 established AD patients to 81 pMCI, which is a label-definition difference. The horizons differ (conversion within 3 years against M18-M48 converters and M48 stables), as do field strength (1.5 T against 3 T) and representation. The rule allows all of these, and they are recorded as candidate explanations.
metric: Accuracy with accuracy and AUC with AUC.

figures.P-185: Linear SVM on the subspace biomarker, 221 MCI (126 pMCI/95 sMCI), 10-fold CV repeated 20 times. Accuracy 69.37%, Wilson with n = 221: z^2/n = 0.0174, centre 0.690, half-width 0.060 -> 0.630-0.751. AUC 0.6951, Hanley-McNeil with 126/95: Q1 = 0.533, Q2 = 0.570, SE = 0.035 -> 0.627-0.763. The original morphological features without subspace learning score 62.92%.
figures.P-41: Heterogeneous ensemble (EfficientNet + ConvNeXt + DenseNet) with attention and a multi-head-attention head. Test set of 15 sMCI + 15 pMCI/AD subjects (Table 1). Accuracy 91.77% +/- 3.14, sensitivity 87.69%, specificity 88.53%, AUC 92.87%. The printed accuracy exceeds both the sensitivity and the specificity, which is impossible on a balanced 15/15 test; those two imply (0.8769 + 0.8853)/2 = 0.881. The same pattern recurs in its other rows, for example 86.76% with 83.65%/81.47%. Wilson with n = 30: 0.918 -> 0.766-0.974; 0.881 -> 0.721-0.955. AUC by Hanley-McNeil with 15/15: Q1 = 0.867, Q2 = 0.894, SE = 0.0505 -> 0.830-1.000.
figures.comparison: Each estimate lies outside the other's interval on accuracy: 0.694 lies below 0.721 even for the implied 0.881, and 0.881 and 0.918 lie above 0.751. The same holds on AUC: 0.695 lies below 0.830, and 0.929 lies above 0.763.

matched_figure_check: Neither paper reports the other's condition. P-41 gives no pMCI-only result without the 15 AD patients and no ROI-feature model, and P-185 has no slice-based model. But P-41's own ablation on the same 30 test subjects places its gap in its architecture. Its single-backbone, single-plane models without attention score 47.67-77.76% accuracy and AUC 0.53-0.80. For example, EfficientNet with the MHA head scores 68.86% (AUC 0.684) on the axial plane and 77.76% (AUC 0.798) on the sagittal plane, which brackets P-185's 69.37%/0.6951, and P-185's own plain-feature baseline is 62.92%. The rise to 91.77%/0.929 comes with the attention modules and the three-backbone, three-plane ensemble. As in C-147, it is the operator's call whether a within-paper ablation counts, under condition 3, as a paper showing an explanation to be sufficient. If it does not, the pair qualifies.
performance_validity: Passes as written: P-41's AUC of 0.929 and accuracy of 0.918 are below 0.97, and P-185's figures are far below. P-41 evaluates on a single 30-subject test set with no external cohort. Its accuracies are arithmetically inconsistent with its own sensitivity and specificity throughout its results tables. Both points are recorded as candidate explanations (precision and reporting reliability), not as the exclusion.

candidate_explanations.difference: Architecture and representation: an attention-augmented, multi-plane CNN ensemble on 2D slices, against a linear SVM on regional thickness and volume. P-41's own simpler models reach P-185's level.
candidate_explanations.quote: The MHA classifier performed even better, achieving an accuracy of 68.86% in the axial plane (AUC:68.37%), 67.85% in the coronal plane (AUC:71.47%), and 77.76% in the sagittal plane (AUC:79.79%)

candidate_explanations.difference: Label definition: 15 patients with established AD are added to P-41's positive class, making part of the task AD against MCI.
candidate_explanations.quote: Furthermore, we added 15 patients with AD to the pMCI group to help the model learn both the progressive and fully diseased brain patterns simultaneously.

candidate_explanations.difference: Horizon: conversion within 3 years, against conversion between M18 and M48 with stability to M48.
candidate_explanations.quote: The second group (pMCI) included 81 participants who were diagnosed with MCI at baseline but progressed to AD within 2.5 years, between month 18 (M18) and M48.

candidate_explanations.difference: Test size and validation: a single 15 + 15 subject test set, against 20 repetitions of 10-fold CV on 221 MCI.
Field strength and ADNI phase: 1.5 T scans against 3 T MPRAGE.
candidate_explanations.quote: We use baseline MRI scans (1.5 T, 1:25 mm × 1:25 mm in-plane spatial resolution, 1.2 mm thick slices) of 528 subjects

candidate_explanations.difference: Reporting reliability: P-41's printed accuracies exceed both its sensitivity and its specificity.
candidate_explanations.quote: The MHA classifier in the same heterogeneous ensemble outperformed the LSTM with an accuracy of 91.77% ±3.14, sensitivity of 87.69% ±3.24, specificity of 88.53% ±3.53, and an impressive AUC of 92.87% ±3.58.

reason: The pair meets conditions 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6. Both papers predict conversion in ADNI MCI from baseline sMRI, and P-41's accuracy and AUC (even at the 0.881 its own sensitivity and specificity imply) and P-185's 69.37%/0.6951 exclude each other in both directions. Neither figure is near ceiling. But P-41's single-plane models without attention score 67-78% (AUC 0.68-0.80) on the same test subjects, which brackets P-185, so P-41's own ablation places the gap in its ensemble and attention architecture. As in C-147, whether that counts as a paper showing the explanation to be sufficient (condition 3) is the operator's call. If it does not, the pair qualifies. None of the other candidate explanations (AD patients in the positive class, horizon, a 30-subject test, field strength) is shown to be sufficient.

quotes.quote: According to whether the MCI subjects will convert to AD or not within a given time period (i.e., 3 years), they are separated into two categories: progressive MCI (pMCI) and stable MCI (sMCI).
Moreover, the 221 MCI subjects contain 126 pMCI and 95 sMCI subjects.
repeated 10-fold cross-validation 20 times to report the average results for each method.
The proposed biomarker achieved highest accuracy of 69.37% when using SVM classifier with linear kernel.
Furthermore, we added 15 patients with AD to the pMCI group to help the model learn both the progressive and fully diseased brain patterns simultaneously.
The dataset was carefully partitioned to ensure that no data leakage occurred, and all results reported in this study were based on the test set.
The MHA classifier performed even better, achieving an accuracy of 68.86% in the axial plane (AUC:68.37%), 67.85% in the coronal plane (AUC:71.47%), and 77.76% in the sagittal plane (AUC:79.79%)

When the attention module was incorporated, the model demonstrated significant improvement, reaching an accuracy of 86.76% ±4.28, sensitivity of 83.65% ±3.86, specificity of 81.47% ±4.12, and an AUC of 88.79% ±4.58.

The MHA classifier in the same heterogeneous ensemble outperformed the LSTM with an accuracy of 91.77% ±3.14, sensitivity of 87.69% ±3.24, specificity of 88.53% ±3.53, and an impressive AUC of 92.87% ±3.58.
